title: Hubble: Decagon Around Saturn's South Pole
explanation:
# Saturn's Mysterious Geometric Poles

Saturn's north and south poles are crowned with strikingly different geometric cloud patterns—a 6-sided hexagon that has remained eerily stable for over 40 years and a newly discovered 10-sided decagon at the south pole—both likely sculpted by invisible waves created where fast-moving upper-atmosphere winds collide with slower winds near the poles. Hubble Space Telescope observations reveal these shapes most clearly in the dark, swirling bands of clouds circling each pole, presenting one of the solar system's most puzzling natural phenomena and a mystery that astronomers are still working to fully understand.
